Goodbye, Fr Ross! This weekend it was time to say goodbye to a great friend of St George Fr Ross Bullock from St Patricks parish in Woolston. Fr Ross as well as helping out with Mass and Confessions during the year was a regular visitor to the school each Friday. Coming into to visit the staff and students Fr Ross provided support to the school in many different ways. In particular he was a great help to the Chaplaincy and RE dept over the years since he had arrived at Woolston in 2019. Providing spiritual direction and support to Mr Walford and the chaplaincy team Fr Ross was a great ally of St George. We are very grateful for all his time spent with us and he will be missed greatly by us all. We wish Fr Ross a restful sabbatical year and remember him in our prayers. Thank you Fr Ross.

We're sure you'll agree that our Year 11s looked amazing for their Prom last week.
As part of our Day of Faith, Year 9 students took part in a creative workshop led by Mrs Gilbank and Miss Gillings. Using a range of technology resources, students worked collaboratively to create a striking piece of string art spelling the word "ASPIRE". Each student took turns carefully hammering in the nails and connecting the yarn to form the finished design. The artwork carries a special meaning for our school community. The individual nails represent the students and staff of Saint George, while the interwoven yarn symbolises the shared values that unite us and enable us to create something truly beautiful together. The completed artwork was proudly displayed beside the altar during Mass. We are extremely proud of the creativity, teamwork and care shown by our students, and the final piece is a wonderful reflection of our community and values.
The Summer Edition We have now reached our 10th and final edition of the academic year. I want to take one last opportunity to thank all of the incredible young journalists who have created a variety of informative and entertaining articles for your reading pleasure. School is a very busy time, so to take on the additional responsibility of sourcing and writing stories in their own free time really is a credit to the level of dedication these students have. Enjoy the long breakmay it be both adventurous and restful. We look forward to reporting back to you in September. Best wishes, Mr J Scott

Meet the Governor: Mike Wood Mike is one of our newest members of the governing board starting as a Foundation Governor in January 2025. He is our SEN Link Governor. He comes with 37 years of teaching experience, working in education as a Geography teacher; Head of department; leader of gifted students and examiner. He is a member of St Boniface Catholic Church is Southampton and at present is Chair of the PPC as well as helping run the music ministry within the church. He has strong connections with St Georges Catholic college. His son attended St Georges and also worked here. Two of his daughters have also worked at the college whilst his wife was a governor in the past. We are excited to see how Mike can support the governing body in the years to come.
On Monday the 22nd of June the Business department took two groups of year 9 students for the final of the Solent Business Challenge against other secondary schools in the city. As always they represented the school fantastically and it's great to see their learning put into action!
A huge thank you to Kier Group for hosting an incredible 3-day virtual/hybrid work experience programme for our Year 10 students this week. The programme provided our students with a fantastic insight into the construction industry, introducing them to a wide range of career pathways and the many exciting opportunities available within the sector. The programme also gave students the chance to build their employability skills, ask questions, and discover the many different roles that contribute to successful construction projectsfrom engineering and site management to design, sustainability, digital technologies and business support. We are so grateful to the KIER team for investing their time, expertise and enthusiasm in supporting the next generation. Computer Science
Our curriculum is designed to enable our pupils to acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to thrive in the information age. We aim to provide a broad and balanced curriculum that includes IT, Computing and Digital literacy. We acknowledge that our pupils come with experiences of using ICT outside the classroom.
Through an innovative and challenging curriculum, we turn their knowledge and skills into an ICT qualification that prepares them for life beyond school. Students have five lessons a fortnight.
Key Stage 3
In Years 7 and 8, the department gives students the opportunity to study computer science and experience computer science in three areas, including digital literacy, information technology and computing, as recommended by the Department for Education to lay the foundation and prepare students for their learning and options choice for GCSE.
In Year 9, pupils study a wide range of topics to prepare them for GCSE studies at Key Stage 4. This also develops computing and ICT skills that can be transferred to other subjects, extending their learning across the curriculum. The topics include:
Spreadsheet modelling
Computer hardware and software
Introduction to Python
Understanding computers
Computer crime and cybersecurity
Networks
HTML and web development
Key Stage 4
The Computer Science department offers two pathways. Pupils have the option to study computer science or the BTEC in Digital information technology.
BTEC in Digital Information Technology
The BTEC in Digital Information Technology offers pupils the opportunity to investigate and demonstrate their understanding of the digital world. Pupils will explore:
User interface principles and project planning techniques
Collecting, presenting and interpreting data
Effective digital working practices.
Computer Science
In computer science, pupils will study computer systems and computational thinking, algorithms and programming:
Computer Science Curriculum Map
Systems architecture
Memory and storage
Computer networks, connections and protocols
Network security
Systems software
Algorithms
Programming fundamentals
Producing robust programmes
Boolean logic
Programming languages and Integrated

pageCache.text:
Open Mornings and Evening 2026
We warmly invite prospective parents and families to our Open Evening on Thursday 1st October 2026 from 5pm to 8pm. This is a wonderful opportunity to explore our school, meet our dedicated staff and pupils, and discover what makes our school such a special place to learn and grow. We look forward to welcoming you and sharing everything our school has to offer.
Open Mornings will be held on Monday 28 September and Wednesday 30 September, from 9.15am to 10.15am. Attendance is by advance booking only.
To reserve a place, please email the Head’s PA at headpa@stgcc.co.uk. Places are limited, so early booking is recommended.
Open Evening 2026 Information

Art
Our Art students are taught in a progressive manner with targets set on an individual basis. We actively encourage independent thinking and problem-solving and strive for individual creativity. There is no house style and our staff are encouraged to contribute their individual skills to the character and work of the department. As a consequence, we create an environment that is forward-thinking and adaptable to the needs of the contemporary education and art worlds. At Key Stage 3, pupils follow a broad, fine art curriculum that covers drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture (including ceramics) and contextual studies. At Key Stage 4, all students follow the AQA syllabus for Art & Design. The course is structured to allow students to work to their individual strengths, while underpinning their performance with sound technical skills and a developing cultural and critical understanding. Students are required to build a body of work that includes sketchbooks as coursework. They have two coursework projects to complete (60%) and an externally set assignment with a 10-hour exam (worth 40% and undertaken over two days).

Business
Year 9
In Year 9, students are introduced to Business with an initial study of businesses in the local area with the aim of identifying and planning a new local business idea. Throughout the year, students cover a range of topics taken from the BTEC Tech Award in Enterprise and the GCSE Business programmes of studies, providing them with an understanding of a broad range of business activities. The main areas of focus are on business in the real world, with a number of topics supporting the learning, including: purpose and nature of business, business ownership, setting business aims and objectives, stakeholders, business location, business planning and expanding a business. There are lots of opportunities for students to take on business-related tasks, such as designing a new business idea and presenting it in front of the ‘dragons’.
Year 10 & 11 Business
In Years 10 and 11, students have the opportunity to develop their knowledge of business by gaining either the BTEC TECH Award in Enterprise or the GCSE Business Studies qualification. Both courses provide exciting challenges where learners’ academic levels can be accommodated through the GCSE or vocational option. You need to be committed, enthusiastic and determined to meet all the deadlines, and confident to deliver speeches and pitches in front of people, whilst working extremely well with others.
Future Pathway
Students may go on to study Level 3 Extended Diploma in Business or A-levels, providing he/she has high GCSE grades in this as well in other subjects. Future careers could be a business teacher; various roles within the business sector, banking, entrepreneurship and many others.
